cards.title: TorchNeuron Makes AWS Trainium a Native PyTorch Device, Boosting HF Model Coverage to 89%
cards.why_it_matters: If you train or serve models on AWS Trainium, this replaces the XLA-based Optimum Neuron workflow with native eager execution, FSDP2, and direct compatibility with Transformers, Diffusers, PEFT, and TRL — no custom modeling classes needed.
cards.summary: TorchNeuron (public beta Oct 20, 2026, pip-installable) adds Trainium as a native PyTorch device with eager mode, torch.compile, DTensor, and FSDP2. Supported text-generation architectures jump from 46% (Optimum Neuron v0.4.5) to 89% of the top-100 most-used models. HF recommends migrating away from Optimum Neuron to use Transformers/Accelerate/TRL directly via device_map='neuron'.

cards.title: Apertus 1.5: Fully Open 8B/70B Models with Native Multimodal, 262k Context, and Thinking Mode
cards.why_it_matters: A significant fully-open release (weights, data, training details) adding multimodality via early-fusion discrete tokenization, long context, and RLVR-based reasoning — directly comparable infrastructure to leading proprietary models for researchers who need reproducible baselines.
cards.summary: Apertus 1.5 continues pretraining Apertus 1.0 with 4T additional tokens (8B) and 2T (70B), reaching 19T and 17T total. Multimodality is added via early-fusion discrete tokens: images use the Emu3.5 tokenizer (1,024 tokens per 512×512 image), audio uses WavTokenizer (40 tokens/sec). Context grows to 262,144 tokens. Post-training pipeline: SFT → long-context SFT → RLVR (~350k prompts) → DPO → charter-aligned SDPO. All weights, data, and SFT/preference mixes are released.

cards.title: Halcyon: Strong Text-to-Image Generation from Scratch, No Language Pretraining Required
cards.why_it_matters: Challenges a core assumption in T2I system design — that internet-scale language pretraining is necessary — with controlled experiments and compute-efficient results that reframe how multimodal models should be pretrained.
cards.summary: Halcyon, a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models trained from scratch on 100M image-text pairs (GPIC dataset), outperforms LlamaGen-XL/8 (48.0 vs 63.3 gFD) with 18.2× less compute at 0.52B parameters, and outperforms JiT-T2I-XXL/8++ (35.3 vs 41.0 gFD) with 275× less compute at 1.6B. Controlled experiments show text-only pretraining does not improve T2I quality. Code and models released.

cards.title: OpenVLHarness: Multimodal Tool-Use Harness Adds 9.7–12.6 Points Across 22 Benchmarks
cards.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to agent and reasoning research: demonstrates that persistent multimodal memory and heterogeneous tool integration close gaps that scaling inference compute alone cannot, with results across eight open and proprietary backbones.
cards.summary: OpenVLHarness combines a capability layer (tool interfaces plus evidence rendering) with persistent multimodal memory storing images, structured data, and web references as addressable artifacts. Evaluated on 22 benchmarks, it improves average scores by 9.7–12.6 points over no-tool baselines, including +11.2 with Qwen3-VL-8B, +9.7 with Kimi K3, and +9.9 with GPT-6 Astra. GPT-6 Luna at medium effort beats Codex and Visual Sketchpad at maximum effort by 7.7–8.5 points at ≤37% token cost.

cards.title: FunCAD-Harness: LLM Agents for Functional CAD Design with Physics-Simulation Feedback
cards.why_it_matters: Relevant to researchers studying LLM agents on structured, verifiable tasks — the simulation-in-the-loop eval framework and 46-mechanism benchmark expose failure modes invisible to visual or static code checks.
cards.summary: FunCAD-Harness translates abstract functional requirements into candidate-specific physical simulation tests, using simulation feedback to guide iterative design revisions by LLM agents. FunCADBench covers 46 mechanism families with interdependent, multi-step operations. Experiments show the harness exposes mechanical failures invisible to visual inspection and substantially improves functional success rates over standard simulation-augmented baselines.

cards.title: CoopUQ: Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Occupancy Forecasting for Multi-Robot Navigation
cards.why_it_matters: Niche but technically substantive for researchers working on multi-agent RL or robot safety: the uncertainty-penalized cost in constrained MARL is a concrete mechanism for handling OOD distribution shift in shared environments.
cards.summary: CoopUQ fuses spatiotemporal features across robots to predict future occupancy grid maps, then uses both predictions and their uncertainty as cost signals in constrained multi-agent RL, penalizing navigation through occupied or highly uncertain regions. Evaluated in Unity3D simulations across varied layouts, pedestrian densities, and OOD rushing behavior, plus real-robot experiments, it shows improved prediction and safety over representative baselines.
